title: European Stocks Steady as Investor Focus Shifts to Economic Data
summary: European stocks were steady at the start of the week amid thin volumes, with traders looking to data for clues about the health of the region’s economy.

title: NYU's Suzy Welch on Career Ambition & Gen Z's Work Paradox
summary: NYU Stern professor Suzy Welch examines a growing contradiction among Gen Z: young workers increasingly value achievement and career success while also wanting to spend less of their lives at work. Welch discusses shifting attitudes toward ambition, work-life balance and what the trend means for employers. She speaks with Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: German Finance Chief Says Trump Is to Blame for Surging Yields
summary: Germany’s finance minister said President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, which has thrown global energy supplies off balance, was responsible for a surge in bond yields across world markets.

title: JPMorgan’s Berro Says Bond Market Can Handle High-Grade Stampede
summary: The US investment-grade bond market faces a busy September, but demand for corporate debt suggests anxiety about heavy supply may be overblown, according to Kelsey Berro, a portfolio manager at JPMorgan Asset Management.

title: US Economy Can Keep Growing Despite Higher Rates, Says House
summary: Wells Fargo’s Sarah House says Chair Kevin Warsh may use Jackson Hole to focus on longer-term questions facing the Federal Reserve rather than signal the next move on interest rates. She also discusses alternative economic data, the Fed balance sheet, Treasury yields and why the U.S. economy continues to show resilience. House speaks with Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney on Surveillance Radio. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Stocks Decline as Nvidia Earnings, Jackson Hole Loom
summary: US stocks fell on Monday as investors geared up for a busy week of economic data and earnings from Nvidia Corp.

title: Treasury Buybacks Are Not 'QE Lite,' Claudia Sahm Argues
summary: Claudia Sahm, New Century Advisors chief economist, argues that the US Treasury's strategic debt buyback operations will only have a temporary, limited impact on markets. She speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Qiagen Names Jonathan Pratt as CEO as Sale Talks Progress
summary: Qiagen NV has appointed Jonathan Pratt as its new chief executive officer, as talks with private equity firms about a possible sale of the European molecular testing company progress.

title: Citadel Securities Calls Treasury Buyback ‘Financial Repression’
summary: The Treasury Department’s efforts to restrain long-term borrowing costs through bond buybacks amount to “financial repression” that risks weakening the dollar and fueling inflation, according to Citadel Securities.

title: Chip Rout Pulls Stocks Down at Start of Busy Week: Markets Wrap
summary: Technology stocks dragged down the equity market in a risk-off start to a week stacked with high-stakes geopolitical and economic events.

title: Central Bankers Don’t Work for Presidents
summary: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Daniel Moss says central banks need enough independence to make painful economic decisions, but autonomy cannot mean freedom from consequences. They ultimately answer to the public, not one president. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 24
summary: Oil dropped after two weeks of gains, with the market waiting to asses the US economic isolation plan for Iran due to be unveiled later Monday.

title: Shipping Oil Through Hormuz Costs $20 Million, Total CEO Says
summary: The cost of shipping oil cargoes on a supertanker through the Strait of Hormuz is about $20 million, the boss of TotalEnergies SE said, underscoring the wide margins to be made by traders and shipowners.

title: Dollar (USD) Outlook: What Is the ‘Debasement Trade’ and Why Does It Matter?
summary: Political and fiscal uncertainty in the US is prompting investors to again turn nervous toward the dollar. As some have offloaded the currency, alternative assets such as Bitcoin and gold have seen their value soar.

title: US-Canada Tariff War Escalates After Collapse of Talks
summary: Brian Gardner, chief Washington policy strategist at Stifel, discusses the collapse in trade negotiations between the US and Canada. The US implemented a new 50% tax on imports of hundreds of Canadian items including furniture, plastics, plywood and electrical equipment on Saturday. He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Canadian Stocks Whipsaw After US Trade Talks Break Down
summary: Canadian stocks flipped between gains and losses at Monday’s open after the collapse of talks with the US unleashed what threatens to become a widening trade war, with Prime Minister Mark Carney recalling his negotiators from Washington.

title: Bessent Eyes Treasury Cash Pile for Debt Buybacks, CNBC Says
summary: The US Treasury could draw down some of its cash pile to fund buybacks of higher-yielding older securities in a bid to tackle rising borrowing costs, CNBC reported Monday, citing two senior departmental officials.

title: Treasuries Gain With Bessent and Warsh Due to Set Direction
summary: Treasuries gained at the start of a potentially pivotal week for the US bond market, with remarks from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh likely to determine where yields go next.

title: Guggenheim's Walsh Says Accounting Was 'Appropriate' at GPI Unit
summary: Guggenheim Partners is working with regulators as they probe a business accounting issue at one of its subsidiaries, according to Anne Walsh, chief investment officer of the firm’s asset-management business. Walsh says the firm is cooperating with regulators. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Natural Gas Rises on Record-Breaking Heat, Lower Output
summary: US natural gas increased, extending gains from the previous session, as forecasts shifted hotter over the weekend, indicating higher demand for the power-plant fuel as consumers ramp up their air-conditioning use. The month is now on track to eclipse 2007 for the hottest population-weighted August on record, according to the private forecaster Commodity Weather Group.
